name: Norwegian Coastal Current
scope: OSW southern Norwegian Skagerrak approach to the Ingoy section at the Barents Sea entrance, following a simplified offshore coastal corridor. Excludes Baltic source-water transit, Jutland inflow, fjord circuits, offshore Norwegian Atlantic Current branches, West Spitsbergen and downstream Murman continuation. No whole connected-system length.
layer: Buoyant coastal-water naming context; no depth-specific core, full transverse section or uniform salinity footprint reconstructed.
time_convention: Regional geography described by Christensen et al. (2026), with Ingoy context from Skagseth et al. (2011). Not a dated observed track, annual mean axis or seasonal geometry series.
source_locator: Section 1 Introduction: Norwegian Coastal Current originates in Skagerrak and flows along Norway into Barents Sea; explicitly distinguished from warm saline Norwegian Atlantic Current.
source_citation: Christensen et al. (2026), Norkyst version 3: the coastal ocean forecasting system for Norway, Geoscientific Model Development 19, 2785-2798, doi:10.5194/gmd-19-2785-2026.

supporting_sources.citation: Skagseth, Drinkwater and Terrile (2011), Wind- and buoyancy-induced transport of the Norwegian Coastal Current in the Barents Sea, JGR Oceans 116, doi:10.1029/2011JC006996.
supporting_sources.locator: Introduction paragraphs 3-7 and Figure 2: source-water convention, coastal route and complex Tromsoflaket pathways converging near Ingoy; data section distinguishes local measurements.
supporting_sources.role: Ingoy gate context and continuity caveat; no drifter trajectory or velocity field digitized.

coordinate_selection: All offshore vertices and approach gates are OSW-selected from named regional geography. Southern gate samples Norwegian Skagerrak approach, not Baltic origin. Alternative Skagerrak/Ingoy approaches test endpoint convention; intermediate coastal detours simplify banks and island passages and require bathymetric review. No source model grid or figure arrows digitized; qualitative seasonal descriptions do not supply annual length or width extremes.

alternative_routes.interpretation: Selected shorter approaches in same regional corridor, not seasonal contraction.

scenario_rule: Two OSW regional approach conventions crossed with longitude and independent endpoint latitude offsets -0.05/0/+0.05 degrees: 54 editorial scenarios, not annual variation or confidence intervals.
